source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the failed check areas and list them clearly.
3. Include reference to specific accessibility standards (e.g., ADA guidelines, local building codes).
4. Note the building component or features that were not compliant, e.g., door width, ramp slope, tactile signs, accessible counter heights, parking spaces.
5. Detail the observations made, providing measurements, photos, or videos as supporting evidence.
6. Describe the impact of the failed check on accessibility, e.g., "A person in a wheelchair cannot access the main entrance because the door width is only 28 inches (ADA requirements specify a minimum width of 32 inches)".
7. Include the date and time of the inspection.
8. Record the names of the inspector and any other parties present during the inspection.
9. Summarize the required corrective actions.
10. Attach any additional reports or documentation related to the failure.
11. Provide the contact information for the property owner or responsible party if
